passages.title: Hannah prays and dedicates Samuel
passages.summary: Hannah endures Peninnah’s provocation, prays at Shiloh, and later brings Samuel to serve there. Hannah speaks from deep grief. She brings that grief to God in prayer.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church lesson studies Hannah's prayer during grief and her trust in God.

passages.title: Hannah’s song and the failure of Eli’s sons
passages.summary: Hannah praises God. Hophni and Phinehas abuse their office. An unnamed messenger announces judgment against Eli’s household. Hannah sings about God helping poor and weak people. Eli's sons instead use power for themselves.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older Church manual connects Hannah's song with Jesus Christ.

passages.title: Samuel hears the call
passages.summary: Samuel repeatedly mistakes the call for Eli’s voice. Eli guides his response, and Samuel receives a difficult message. Samuel learns to listen and speak a hard message. Eli must hear judgment against his family.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects Samuel’s response with learning to recognize revelation.

passages.title: The ark is captured and Eli’s household suffers loss
passages.summary: Israel brings the ark from Shiloh into battle. The Philistines capture it. Eli and his sons die, and Ichabod is born. The losses affect a whole household. Ichabod’s unnamed mother expresses the catastrophe while dying after childbirth.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church lesson examines trust in the ark. Why does carrying the ark fail to protect the army?

passages.title: The ark among the Philistine towns
passages.summary: The ark is placed beside Dagon at Ashdod. Distress follows its movement to Gath and Ekron. The Philistines capture the ark but cannot control God. Their idol falls, and their towns suffer.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual connects the ark’s troubles with Israel’s need to honor God.

passages.title: The ark returns to Beth Shemesh
passages.summary: The Philistines send offerings with the ark on a cart. It reaches Beth Shemesh, where rejoicing gives way to mourning. The people of Beth Shemesh welcome the ark. Joy turns to fear after people die.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church lesson uses these events to study trust and obedience.

passages.title: Samuel leads the gathering at Mizpah
passages.summary: The ark stays with Abinadab’s household. Samuel calls Israel to renewed worship and leads the gathering at Mizpah. The memorial stone marks received help. Samuel’s circuit combines worship, leadership, and judgment.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies turning toward God after earlier failure.

passages.title: The people request a king
passages.summary: Samuel’s sons take bribes. Israel’s elders ask for a king. Samuel warns that kings take people, land, and goods. The demand responds to real leadership failures. The warning asks readers to consider the costs of concentrated power.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church lesson invites readers to consider Jesus Christ as their King.

passages.title: Saul searches for donkeys and meets Samuel
passages.summary: Kish sends Saul with a servant to find missing donkeys. Their search brings them to Samuel. Saul sets out to find lost donkeys. The search brings him to Samuel and a new task.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects Saul’s selection with a call to service.

passages.title: Saul is anointed and presented publicly
passages.summary: Samuel anoints Saul privately. Later, Saul is selected before the gathering at Mizpah and found among the baggage. Private anointing and public selection are distinct scenes. Hayes studies their place among differing presentations of kingship.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church lesson connects anointing and changed purpose with service by revelation.

passages.title: Saul relieves Jabesh Gilead
passages.summary: Nahash threatens the people of Jabesh Gilead. Saul gathers help, wins the battle, and refuses to execute earlier opponents. Saul rescues Jabesh Gilead. He then stops supporters from killing people who had opposed him.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual studies Saul’s early leadership and the renewed kingdom.

passages.title: Samuel reviews leadership and covenant responsibility
passages.summary: Samuel asks the people to assess his conduct. He recalls earlier deliverers and warns both people and king to remain faithful. Israel now has a king. Both king and people must still listen to God.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual studies Samuel’s final address and continued prayer for the people.

passages.title: Pressure at Michmash and Saul’s offering
passages.summary: Jonathan attacks a Philistine post. Saul’s men begin to leave. Saul offers a sacrifice before Samuel arrives. Samuel rejects his family’s lasting rule. Saul acts because he fears losing his army. Samuel says he has not kept God’s command.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church lesson studies obedience under pressure. The older manual also reads the offering as unauthorized priesthood action.

passages.title: Jonathan’s attack and Saul’s dangerous oath
passages.summary: Jonathan and his armor bearer attack a garrison. Saul’s food prohibition places Jonathan under sentence of death, but the people rescue him. Saul's oath nearly costs Jonathan his life. The soldiers protect the man who helped them win.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual studies Jonathan’s faith and the harmful effect of Saul’s oath.

passages.title: Amalek, Agag, and Saul’s rejection
passages.summary: Saul attacks Amalek but spares Agag and selected livestock. Samuel rejects Saul’s defense and later kills Agag. Saul spares Agag and valuable animals. Samuel challenges his claim of obedience. The order also calls for killing children.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me asks why obedience matters more than making a religious display.

passages.title: David is anointed and enters Saul’s service
passages.summary: Samuel anoints Jesse’s youngest son David. David later plays music for Saul and serves in his household. God tells Samuel to look beyond a person's size. David later helps Saul through music.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church lesson asks readers to consider a person's heart instead of outward appearance.

passages.title: David faces Goliath in the Valley of Elah
passages.summary: David brings food to his brothers. He accepts Goliath’s challenge and strikes him with a sling. He then uses Goliath’s sword. David trusts God and uses skills learned as a shepherd. He faces a soldier others fear.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me asks how trust in God can give courage during a hard task.

passages.title: Friendship, jealousy, and royal marriage plans
passages.summary: Jonathan forms a bond with David. Saul grows jealous, offers Merab, then arranges David’s marriage to Michal through a deadly demand. Friendship contrasts with treating a person as a threat. The women’s marriages also serve Saul’s political plans.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church lesson compares Jonathan’s support with Saul’s jealousy.

passages.title: Michal helps David escape
passages.summary: Saul resumes attempts to kill David. Michal helps David through a window. David joins Samuel at Ramah, where pursuit is interrupted. Michal takes action in danger. A household idol appears in her deception, complicating a simple picture of household religion.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older Church manual compares Samuel's group of prophets with later Church schools.

passages.title: Jonathan warns David and renews their covenant
passages.summary: Jonathan tests Saul’s intent at the new-moon meal. He signals danger with arrows and parts from David in grief. Their promise extends beyond immediate friendship to their households. Saul’s attack also puts Jonathan at risk.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: What does Jonathan risk by protecting David from his father?

passages.title: David seeks food at Nob and refuge at Gath
passages.summary: Ahimelech gives David consecrated bread and Goliath’s sword. Doeg observes him. David then escapes danger at Achish’s court. David’s misleading claim about a royal mission places others in danger. Need, survival, and responsibility all matter.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual connects the bread account with Jesus’s later teaching about human need.

passages.title: David gathers followers and Saul orders the Nob massacre
passages.summary: David gathers distressed followers and seeks safety for his parents. Saul orders the priests’ deaths. Doeg carries out the killing, and Abiathar escapes. The guards refuse the order, but Doeg acts. The massacre includes children. David acknowledges responsibility for danger to Abiathar’s family.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older Church manual condemns Saul's attack on the priests.

passages.title: Keilah, wilderness pursuit, and Jonathan’s support
passages.summary: David rescues Keilah, leaves after consulting God, and meets Jonathan during Saul’s pursuit. A Philistine attack interrupts the chase. David seeks God's guidance as danger changes. Jonathan visits him and strengthens his trust.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does David respond when the town he saved may hand him over?

passages.title: David spares Saul in the cave
passages.summary: David cuts part of Saul’s robe but refuses to kill him. Afterward he speaks openly, and Saul acknowledges David’s future. David spares Saul but keeps his distance. His restraint does not end Saul's pursuit.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me invites readers to study David's self-control and forgiveness.

passages.title: Abigail prevents David’s revenge
passages.summary: After Nabal refuses assistance, David prepares an attack. Abigail brings provisions and persuades him to stop. After Nabal dies, she marries David. Abigail stops David from killing Nabal’s household. David accepts her correction and thanks God for her help.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church lesson studies restraint and forgiveness. It compares Abigail’s intervention with Jesus Christ.

passages.title: David takes the spear and water jar
passages.summary: David and Abishai enter Saul’s camp. David again refuses to kill Saul, then confronts Abner about the failure to protect him. David again has a chance to kill Saul. He takes Saul’s spear and water jug instead.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies self-control. Restraint and continued separation occur together in the story.

passages.title: David lives under Achish and conceals his raids
passages.summary: David moves with his household and followers into Philistine territory. Achish grants Ziklag. David raids other populations and misleads Achish. Achish trusts David's false reports. People in the raided towns pay for David's secret.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual links David’s raids with earlier commands to take the land. The raids also kill whole households.

passages.title: Saul consults the woman at Endor
passages.summary: Saul seeks help from a woman who calls on the dead. The chapter names Samuel as the speaker who warns him of defeat. Fear drives Saul to a practice he had suppressed. The woman also gives food and care to the distressed king.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual says the speaker was not Samuel. The chapter itself repeatedly calls him Samuel.

passages.title: Philistine leaders send David away
passages.summary: Achish defends David, but the other leaders distrust him in battle against Israel. David and his men are sent back. Achish’s confidence conflicts with the other leaders’ concern. Readers also know about David’s earlier deception.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Why do the Philistine leaders distrust David, even though Achish trusts him?

passages.title: David recovers the captives and shares the spoil
passages.summary: David returns to burned Ziklag. An abandoned Egyptian servant guides the pursuit. David recovers the captives and gives equal shares to those guarding baggage. Care for a sick outsider makes the pursuit possible. David refuses to treat exhausted companions as worthless.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Why does David share recovered goods with people who stayed behind?

passages.title: Saul and his sons die at Gilboa
passages.summary: The Philistines defeat Israel. Jonathan and two brothers die. Saul falls on his sword, and the people of Jabesh Gilead recover the bodies. The ending records loss and dignity after defeat. The people who once received Saul’s help now honor his household.
passages.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: How do the people of Jabesh Gilead honor Saul after his defeat?

lds.text: What does Jonathan risk by protecting David from his father?

events.title: David seeks food at Nob and refuge at Gath
events.summary: Ahimelech gives David consecrated bread and Goliath’s sword. Doeg observes him. David then escapes danger at Achish’s court.
events.detail: David’s misleading claim about a royal mission places others in danger. Need, survival, and responsibility all matter.
events.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual connects the bread account with Jesus’s later teaching about human need.

events.title: David gathers followers and Saul orders the Nob massacre
events.summary: David gathers distressed followers and seeks safety for his parents. Saul orders the priests’ deaths. Doeg carries out the killing, and Abiathar escapes.
events.detail: The guards refuse the order, but Doeg acts. The massacre includes children. David acknowledges responsibility for danger to Abiathar’s family.
events.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older Church manual condemns Saul's attack on the priests.

events.title: Keilah, wilderness pursuit, and Jonathan’s support
events.summary: David rescues Keilah, leaves after consulting God, and meets Jonathan during Saul’s pursuit. A Philistine attack interrupts the chase.
events.detail: David seeks God's guidance as danger changes. Jonathan visits him and strengthens his trust.
events.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does David respond when the town he saved may hand him over?

events.title: David spares Saul in the cave
events.summary: David cuts part of Saul’s robe but refuses to kill him. Afterward he speaks openly, and Saul acknowledges David’s future.
events.detail: David spares Saul but keeps his distance. His restraint does not end Saul's pursuit.
events.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me invites readers to study David's self-control and forgiveness.

events.title: Abigail prevents David’s revenge
events.summary: After Nabal refuses assistance, David prepares an attack. Abigail brings provisions and persuades him to stop. After Nabal dies, she marries David.
events.detail: Abigail stops David from killing Nabal’s household. David accepts her correction and thanks God for her help.
events.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church lesson studies restraint and forgiveness. It compares Abigail’s intervention with Jesus Christ.

events.title: David takes the spear and water jar
events.summary: David and Abishai enter Saul’s camp. David again refuses to kill Saul, then confronts Abner about the failure to protect him.
events.detail: David again has a chance to kill Saul. He takes Saul’s spear and water jug instead.
events.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies self-control. Restraint and continued separation occur together in the story.

events.title: David lives under Achish and conceals his raids
events.summary: David moves with his household and followers into Philistine territory. Achish grants Ziklag. David raids other populations and misleads Achish.
events.detail: Achish trusts David's false reports. People in the raided towns pay for David's secret.
events.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual links David’s raids with earlier commands to take the land. The raids also kill whole households.

events.title: Saul consults the woman at Endor
events.summary: Saul seeks help from a woman who calls on the dead. The chapter names Samuel as the speaker who warns him of defeat.
events.detail: Fear drives Saul to a practice he had suppressed. The woman also gives food and care to the distressed king.
events.uncertainty: Named localities and broad regions only. Camp, cave, household, and road positions remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual says the speaker was not Samuel. The chapter itself repeatedly calls him Samuel.

events.title: Philistine leaders send David away
events.summary: Achish defends David, but the other leaders distrust him in battle against Israel. David and his men are sent back.
events.detail: Achish’s confidence conflicts with the other leaders’ concern. Readers also know about David’s earlier deception.

lds.text: Why do the Philistine leaders distrust David, even though Achish trusts him?

events.title: David recovers the captives and shares the spoil
events.summary: David returns to burned Ziklag. An abandoned Egyptian servant guides the pursuit. David recovers the captives and gives equal shares to those guarding baggage.
events.detail: Care for a sick outsider makes the pursuit possible. David refuses to treat exhausted companions as worthless.

guides.title: Study 1 Samuel
guides.description: Follow selected chapters through the book.

steps.title: Hannah prays and dedicates Samuel
steps.text: Hannah endures Peninnah’s provocation, prays at Shiloh, and later brings Samuel to serve there. Hannah speaks from deep grief. She brings that grief to God in prayer.

steps.title: David is anointed and enters Saul’s service
steps.text: Samuel anoints Jesse’s youngest son David. David later plays music for Saul and serves in his household. God tells Samuel to look beyond a person's size. David later helps Saul through music.

steps.title: Saul and his sons die at Gilboa
steps.text: The Philistines defeat Israel. Jonathan and two brothers die. Saul falls on his sword, and the people of Jabesh Gilead recover the bodies. The ending records loss and dignity after defeat. The people who once received Saul’s help now honor his household.

textRoutes.summary: Hannah endures Peninnah’s provocation, prays at Shiloh, and later brings Samuel to serve there.
textRoutes.detail: Hannah speaks from deep grief. She brings that grief to God in prayer.
